node.content-desc:
Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari has said the government is planning to introduce a "flying bus" as part of its vision to modernise India's transportation system with next-generation mobility solutions.
Speaking at an event in Lucknow, Gadkari described the proposed flying bus as the "next big promise" in urban transport and said it would be part of the government's broader push to adopt advanced technologies.
"Now I am going to bring a bus that flies in the air," the minister said, without disclosing a timeline or technical details of the project.
Notably, Gadkari has previously advocated the adoption of emerging transport technologies, including electric aircraft and drones, as part of India's long-term infrastructure strategy.
The announcement comes amid a renewed row over the nationwide rollout of E20 petrol, with people raising concerns about mileage and compatibility in older vehicles.
Gadkari has rejected allegations of a conflict of interest linked to his family’s businesses, called the criticism politically motivated, and maintained that ethanol blending helps reduce pollution and India’s dependence on imported crude oil.
